articles.title: Bengaluru horror: Man hacks 15-year-old nephew to death over land dispute, surrenders
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Man allegedly hacks 15-year-old nephew to death over ancestral land dispute, then surrenders at police station; accused arrested.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Soladevanahalli police have arrested a man for allegedly murdering his 15-year-old nephew with a deadly weapon while he was sleeping.The accused is Mohan and the deceased teenager is M Krishna, a Class 10 govt school student. Police said Krishna’s father Muniraju alias Murali had died around 12 years back and his mother Puspha had abandoned them around 15 years back. Krishna and his elder brother Yashwanth, a daily wage worker, lived in a small house in Ivarakandapura near Hesaraghatta in Soladevanahalli.Muniraju owned about one acre of ancestral land near Kundana in Devanahalli. Last year, accused Mohan allegedly forged the signatures of Krishna and his brother Yashwanthwithout their knowledge and sold the land to GK Builders, Yelahanka, read the FIR.Following this, the elder sister of Muniraju, Pushpa, filed a complaint at Vishwanathapura police station. When the builders discovered the fraudulent transaction, they transferred payments directly into the bank accounts of Pushpa, Yashwanth and Krishna. Enraged by this financial settlement, Mohan frequently visited the brothers to pick fights and harass them.On Monday around 10pm, Mohan went to Krishna’s house and hacked him to death with a machete. articles.title: Como um fotógrafo fez da gastronomia um negócio de R$ 60 mil por mês | G1
articles.standfirst: Produzindo fotos e vídeos para restaurantes, empreendedor transformou milhões de visualizações nas redes em um negócio de alcance nacional.
articles.summary: Produzindo fotos e vídeos para restaurantes, empreendedor transformou milhões de visualizações nas redes em um negócio de alcance nacional.
articles.body:
Um vídeo de um ovo de Páscoa com quase 2 milhões de visualizações, um hambúrguer que alcançou 8 milhões e uma pizza assistida mais de 15 milhões de vezes.

Apesar dos produtos diferentes, todos têm algo em comum: foram produzidos pelo fotógrafo catarinense Thiago Pinheiro , conhecido como Pinha, que transformou a criação de conteúdo gastronômico em um negócio de alcance nacional .

Dono de um estúdio de fotografia desde 2019, Pinha encontrou durante a pandemia um nicho que mudaria os rumos da empresa.

Com restaurantes e pequenos negócios buscando fortalecer a presença digital, ele passou a se especializar em fotos e vídeos de comida para cardápios online e redes sociais.

“Eu digo que a fotografia gastronômica me escolheu porque muitos negócios precisavam se posicionar, colocar fotos em cardápio para plataformas digitais e trabalhar as redes sociais”, conta o fotógrafo.

Como um fotógrafo fez da gastronomia um negócio de R$ 60 mil por mês — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

O primeiro grande sucesso veio ao lado de uma pequena doceria que funcionava apenas por delivery. Um vídeo produzido para divulgar um ovo de Páscoa viralizou e levou a marca para todo o país.

Segundo Pinha, a repercussão foi tão grande que a empresa ampliou a operação e hoje possui duas lojas físicas.

O impacto também foi sentido no próprio negócio. A visibilidade gerada pelos conteúdos viralizados atraiu clientes de diferentes estados e abriu portas para novos projetos.

“Ganhei notoriedade em nível nacional. Recebemos convites para trabalhar com empresas do Paraná, São Paulo e Rio Grande do Sul”, afirma.

Atualmente, cerca de 65% dos trabalhos realizados pelo estúdio são voltados à gastronomia . Os pacotes de produção de conteúdo partem de R$ 3,2 mil e o negócio registra faturamento mensal de aproximadamente R$ 60 mil .

Para quem busca aumentar o alcance nas redes sociais, o fotógrafo defende uma estratégia que vai além de imagens bonitas. A primeira dica é mostrar os bastidores do negócio e humanizar a marca .

A segunda é explorar elementos visuais que despertem desejo nos consumidores, como queijo derretendo, massas sendo abertas ou hambúrgueres sendo finalizados. Por fim, ele recomenda adaptar tendências das redes sociais à realidade de cada empresa.

O trabalho de Pinha também é reconhecido por clientes. A gerente de marketing Aline Junges afirma que conteúdos produzidos em parceria com o fotógrafo ajudaram a ampliar a exposição da marca.

Para ela, unir espontaneidade e qualidade profissional é um diferencial para atrair consumidores nas plataformas digitais.

Depois de acumular milhões de visualizações e ajudar empresas a ganhar destaque na internet, Pinha diz que o próximo desafio continua sendo o mesmo: usar a produção de conteúdo para impulsionar outros empreendedores.

“É continuar trabalhando com dedicação, ajudando empresas a se posicionar, vender mais e prosperar”, afirma.

articles.body:
Paraná está sob dois alertas de tempestade — Foto: Geraldo Bubniak/AEN

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu dois alertas para tempestades no Paraná nesta quarta-feira (14). Os avisos são válidos até as 23h59.

O alerta mais severo, de perigo para tempestade , atinge 309 cidades. Há previsão de chuvas de até 60 milímetros por hora ou até 100 milímetros no dia, além de ventos que podem chegar aos 100 km/h e chuva de granizo. Veja lista abaixo.

O alerta potencial de tempestade é para todos os 399 municípios do estado, com ventos que podem chegar a 60 km/h e chuva de até 50 milímetros no dia, além da previsão de queda de granizo.

Segundo o Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar), nesta quarta-feira (14), as chuvas ocorrem de moderada a forte intensidade em diversos momentos do dia em todas as regiões.

Por conta do avanço de uma massa de ar mais fria e seca em direção ao Sul do país, os índices de instabilidade entre o Rio Grande do Sul (RS) e o estado paranaense. Desse modo, os eventos severos se concentram predominantemente na metade norte e leste do Paraná.

articles.title: Por que eleições mexem com a bolsa, o dólar e os juros? | G1
articles.standfirst: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.summary: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.body:
A divulgação do resultado do primeiro turno das eleições foi seguida por uma alta da bolsa de valores e uma queda dos juros futuros. Isso não significa que a economia tenha mudado da noite para o dia, mas que bancos, fundos e investidores passaram a reavaliar suas expectativas para os próximos anos.

O mercado financeiro reage não apenas ao que acontece no presente, mas também ao que pode acontecer. Por isso, pesquisas, declarações e resultados eleitorais podem provocar oscilações nos preços de ações, moedas e juros. O cenário internacional e os movimentos de entrada e saída de recursos do país também influenciam.

Essas oscilações refletem as expectativas do mercado, mas não revelam, por si só, a situação da economia. Para entender os possíveis efeitos de cada cenário sobre a população, é preciso considerar também indicadores como emprego, renda, preços e benefícios sociais.

Toda semana, o g1 Explica simplifica a economia, o mercado financeiro e a educação financeira, mostrando como tudo isso afeta o seu bolso.

articles.title: Mega-Sena pode pagar R$ 150 milhões nesta quarta-feira; g1 transmite | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.070 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 150 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre exepcionalmente às 21h desta quarta-feira (14), em São Paulo.

No concurso do último domingo (11), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: MEI pode ter dívida perdoada e receber PIX de R$ 5 mil; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Pacote estabelece critérios para acesso aos benefícios, mas parte das medidas ainda depende de aprovação do Congresso ou de definição das regras pelo governo.
articles.summary: Pacote estabelece critérios para acesso aos benefícios, mas parte das medidas ainda depende de aprovação do Congresso ou de definição das regras pelo governo.
articles.body:
Desenrola Brasil — Foto: Luis Lima Jr./Fotoarena/Estadão Conteúdo

🔎 As propostas incluem perdão de dívidas tributárias , renegociação de débitos bancários e apoio financeiro de até R$ 5 mil para investimentos . O governo também prevê aumentar o teto de faturamento do MEI e simplificar algumas obrigações fiscais.

O anúncio ocorre a 12 dias do segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, quando o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) irá concorrer em busca da reeleição contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O pleito está marcado para 25 de outubro.

Batizado de Prospera MEI, o pacote foi apresentado pelo presidente Lula e por integrantes da equipe econômica. A iniciativa reúne medidas para aliviar dívidas e facilitar o acesso a recursos para quem quer investir e expandir o próprio negócio.

O Brasil tem 17,56 milhões de MEIs ativos, dos quais mais de 3,6 milhões têm pendências com a União. Cerca de 4,1 milhões também estão inscritos no Cadastro Único para Programas Sociais do Governo Federal (CadÚnico), o que evidencia a vulnerabilidade de parte do segmento.

Parte das propostas ainda depende da aprovação do Congresso Nacional, enquanto outras seguem em elaboração pelo governo.

Entenda abaixo o que foi anunciado, quem se beneficia e o que falta para que as medidas saiam do papel.

O governo apresentou cinco medidas principais:

💳 Perdão de dívidas tributárias: para MEIs com débitos inscritos na Dívida Ativa da União;

🤝 Renegociação de dívidas bancárias: por meio do programa Desenrola 3.0;

💰 Criação do PixMEI: com apoio financeiro de até R$ 5 mil;

📈 Aumento do limite de faturamento: para MEIs;

🧾 Dispensa de nota fiscal: em determinadas operações.

O pacote também prevê medidas para ampliar oportunidades de negócios para pequenos empreendedores e reduzir exigências burocráticas.

Apesar de o pacote também mencionar empresas do Simples Nacional, a maioria das medidas anunciadas é voltada aos MEIs.

O perdão das dívidas tributárias, por exemplo, foi desenhado para os microempreendedores que possuem débitos inscritos na Dívida Ativa da União. A proposta de renegociação de dívidas bancárias também tem foco nesse grupo.

O mesmo ocorre com o aumento do teto de faturamento e a possibilidade de contratação de um segundo funcionário.

➡️ Empresas enquadradas como Microempresa (ME) ou Empresa de Pequeno Porte (EPP) também podem ser impactadas por medidas de simplificação e por iniciativas voltadas ao ambiente de negócios.

Quais dívidas poderão ser perdoadas e quem terá direito?

A principal medida do pacote é o envio ao Congresso Nacional de um Projeto de Lei Complementar (PLP) que prevê o perdão integral de dívidas tributárias de MEIs inscritas na Dívida Ativa da União.

🔎 Isso significa que nem todo débito em atraso será automaticamente perdoado. A dívida precisa ter passado pelas etapas administrativas de cobrança e ter sido formalmente inscrita na dívida ativa. (saiba mais abaixo)

A proposta pode beneficiar cerca de 3,6 milhões de microempreendedores e eliminar débitos que somam aproximadamente R$ 12,6 bilhões .

De acordo com o governo, o projeto foi elaborado após avaliações da Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN) apontarem que grande parte desses débitos possui baixa perspectiva de recuperação.

Durante o anúncio, o ministro do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte, Paulo Henrique Pereira, afirmou que o endividamento dos microempreendedores se agravou nos últimos anos.

"Especialmente depois da pandemia, o nível de endividamento dos microempreendedores individuais aumentou muito. Nós tentamos trabalhar muito para reduzir esse endividamento ao longo dos últimos anos [...] mas chegamos à conclusão que ou o Estado brasileiro perdoa a dívida dos MEIs, ou a gente não vai vencer esse mal terrível", declarou.

A proposta ainda depende da aprovação do Congresso. O texto ainda será analisado pelos parlamentares e poderá sofrer alterações durante a tramitação.

A Dívida Ativa da União (DAU) reúne débitos que pessoas físicas e empresas possuem com o governo federal e que não foram pagos dentro do prazo previsto.

Quando a cobrança administrativa não resulta no pagamento, a dívida pode ser inscrita nesse cadastro oficial. A partir desse momento, a cobrança passa para a Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN), que pode adotar medidas administrativas e judiciais para recuperar os valores.

Entre os débitos que podem ser inscritos estão:

impostos e contribuições federais não pagos;

juros, multas e outras obrigações financeiras devidas à União.

A inscrição pode levar a protestos, dificuldades para obter crédito e ações judiciais de cobrança.

O projeto do governo prevê o perdão das dívidas inscritas na Dívida Ativa da União até 13 de outubro de 2026, incluindo os valores principais, juros, multas e encargos legais.

O governo também anunciou uma nova etapa do Desenrola voltada exclusivamente aos MEIs. Segundo o Ministério do Empreendedorismo, esse público acumula cerca de R$ 6 bilhões em dívidas bancárias.

📎 A proposta prevê que o governo compre essas dívidas dos bancos , que deverão oferecer descontos de pelo menos 90% para participar do programa. As instituições que concederem os maiores abatimentos terão prioridade.

Nesta primeira etapa, a negociação será feita diretamente entre o governo e os bancos. Por isso, os MEIs não precisam tomar nenhuma providência. A expectativa é reduzir o peso das dívidas e facilitar a retomada do acesso ao crédito.

Outra medida que chamou atenção foi o anúncio do PixMEI. A proposta prevê a concessão de até R$ 5 mil para investimentos em pequenos negócios.

💵 O recurso será não reembolsável. Ou seja, não precisará ser devolvido pelo beneficiário.

O dinheiro poderá ser usado na compra de equipamentos e ferramentas de trabalho ou na ampliação da estrutura do negócio. A proposta também prevê suporte técnico aos empreendedores, com participação de parceiros como o Sebrae.

O governo ainda não informou quando a iniciativa será lançada, quantos empreendedores serão atendidos, quais serão os critérios para participar, nem qual será o orçamento destinado ao programa.

Por isso, neste momento, não há inscrições abertas nem prazo para solicitar o benefício.

Outra frente do pacote envolve uma proposta já em tramitação no Congresso Nacional. O texto prevê o aumento do teto anual de faturamento do MEI, que atualmente é de R$ 81 mil.

articles.title: 'Pesca fantasma': pesquisa mapeia impactos na fauna marinha em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo é feito no Sul do estado, na área onde vive boto ameaçado de extinção. A expectativa é que o levantamento possa sustentar ações de limpeza, prevenção e conscientização.
articles.summary: Para os pesquisadores, a expectativa é que o levantamento possa sustentar ações de limpeza, prevenção e conscientização.
articles.body:
Uma pesquisa universitária busca entender os impactos na fauna marinha causados pela chamada "pesca fantasma". O fenômeno ocorre quando redes, linhas e outros equipamentos de pesca são perdidos ou abandonados no mar ou em rios, e continuam capturando e matando animais mesmo sem a presença de pescadores.

O estudo é feito como Trabalho de Conclusão de Curso (TCC) da aluna Nicole Pereira de Moura, do curso de ciências biológicas da Universidade do Extremo Sul Catarinense ( Unesc ), em Criciúma , no Sul de Santa Catarina.

Moradora de Torres, cidade litorânea gaúcha na divisa com Santa Catarina, ela passou a investigar o tema após notar a presença constante de redes abandonadas enquanto caminhava pela praia.

A presença desse tipo de material preocupa especialistas porque o Sul do estado habitat dos botos-de-Lahille (Tursiops gephyreus), espécie ameaçada de extinção, que voltou a ser avistada na região após 20 anos (veja mais abaixo).

Nicole explicou o conceito de "pesca fantasma":

"Pesca fantasma é um fenômeno em que equipamentos de pesca, quando são soltos no ambiente e ali permanecem por longos períodos, continuam podendo capturar organismos. Pescando, gerando a mortalidade de diferentes grupos de animais. E é um problema emergente, global, que afeta peixes, tartarugas, invertebrados e também mamíferos marinhos, como as baleias e os golfinhos".

Ela destacou ainda que redes de pesca abandonadas na areia, por exemplo, podem voltar para o mar com a ressaca. Aquelas que são perdidas na água também têm potencial de capturar animais, mesmo sem o pescador por perto.

➡️ Desde abril, Nicole e o professor orientador, Rodrigo Machado, percorrem trechos na praia na região em busca de redes de pesca abandonadas.

Eles escolhem um pedaço entre a foz do Rio Mampituba e a barra do Rio Araranguá . Um caminho de 1 quilômetro é percorrido pela dupla e os dois contabilizam quantos apetrechos são encontrados abandonados.

Ao achar uma rede, eles anotam as características dela e verificam se algum animal ficou preso nela.

Ao longo desse período, os pesquisadores já identificaram mais de 100 fragmentos de redes de pesca no Sul do estado.

"Já encontramos uma rede inteira com 11 siris e seis peixes, o que evidencia a 'pesca fantasma'", declarou a estudante.

Estudante Nicole e professor orientador Rodrigo analisam redes de pesca abandonadas em praias do Sul de SC — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

Pesquisadores querem que trabalho ajude a sustentar ações de conscientização

No Sul do estado, onde a pesquisa é feita, a preocupação é com uma espécie específica: nesse trecho, estão os botos-de-Lahille.

Eles fazem parte da lista de animais ameaçados de extinção e voltaram a aparecer no local depois de 20 anos.

A pesquisa é feita em parceria com o projeto Botos de Araranguá, também executado pela Unesc, que monitora a presença da espécie.

Boto-de-Lahille no Rio Araranguá — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

O professor explicou que a população de botos mora na cidade de Passo de Torres , na divisa com o Rio Grande do Sul, e, nos meses mais quentes, aparece mais também em outra municípios do Sul de Santa Catarina.

A expectativa dos pesquisadores é que o levantamento embase políticas de limpeza, prevenção e conscientização ambiental.

"A gente não consegue medir diretamente o potencial de captura dessas redes, mas, expondo esses resultados, a gente discute aliado a registros já documentados de emalhamento da espécie com redes de pesca parecidas com as que a gente está encontrando na praia", declarou a estudante.

A Prefeitura de Macaé, por meio da Secretaria de Saúde, realiza no dia 21 de outubro uma programação especial no Polo Municipal de Oncologia em alusão às campanhas Outubro Rosa e Novembro Azul. A atividade acontece das 8h às 13h na própria unidade, combinando orientações médicas, momentos de acolhimento, lazer e cuidados com a autoestima voltados aos pacientes, familiares e profissionais de saúde.

A iniciativa busca sensibilizar a população sobre a importância da prevenção e do diagnóstico precoce do câncer de mama e de próstata, além de incentivar hábitos de vida saudáveis. A estrutura do Polo oferece atendimento especializado contínuo, contando com suporte médico, psicólogos, nutricionistas, assistentes sociais, fonoaudiólogos, fisioterapeutas e farmacêuticos ao longo de todas as etapas do tratamento.

A programação terá início às 8h com recepção musical e abertura oficial. Ao longo da manhã, o público participante contará com sessões de massoterapia, oficina de maquiagem em parceria com o projeto Oncorenascer, desfile temático e atividades corporais conduzidas por fisioterapeutas.

O evento inclui também palestras sobre a saúde da mulher e os cuidados diários do paciente oncológico, ministradas por médicos da rede municipal. A manhã será finalizada com um momento de confraternização, seguido por um bingo recreativo e encerramento com atrações culturais

articles.title: James Spader volta como Ultron em VisionQuest; ator fala ao g1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Sem atuar desde 2023, ator americano fala ao g1 sobre retornar ao robô Ultron após dez anos: 'Eu me diverti ainda mais'. Série continuação de 'WandaVision' estreou nesta terça (13).
articles.summary: Em entrevista ao g1, James Spader detalha sua volta como Ultron em VisionQuest e a experiência de atuar na nova série da Marvel para o Disney+.
articles.body:
Mais do que o retorno do super-herói sintético da Marvel, "VisionQuest" é também a volta de um dos maiores vilões do Universo Cinematográfico da editora – e de um dos melhores intérpretes.

Vencedor de três prêmios Emmy, o principal da televisão americana, James Spader aparece mais uma vez como o robô maligno Ultron, mais de dez anos depois de "Vingadores: Era de Ultron" (2015).

Dois dos oito episódios estão disponíveis desde terça-feira (13) na plataforma de streaming Disney+ (que adiantou a data do lançamento em um dia).

Espécie de conclusão de trilogia, que teve como precursoras "WandaVision" , de 2021, e "Agatha all along", de 2024, "VisionQuest" foca na história do personagem interpretado por Paul Bettany.

Ou pelo menos uma versão dele. Reconstruído ao final da série de cinco anos atrás, sem memórias ou as ligações que faziam dele um herói, o novo Visão busca a ajuda de outras inteligências artificiais para recuperar a ligação com a própria humanidade esquecida.

James Spader e Paul Bettany em cena de 'VisionQuest' — Foto: Divulgação

Entre elas, claro, está a entidade por trás de sua criação. Robô maligno que quase destruiu o planeta, Ultron habita o sótão de uma casa construída na mente do protagonista – onde, inclusive, é forçado a usar como avatar uma aparência de carne e osso muito parecida com Spader.

"A primeira pergunta que me fiz foi: onde está esse Visão agora? Com quem ele está conversando? Ele está passando por uma crise de identidade. E, imediatamente — por qualquer motivo que seja, talvez apenas por eu ser um grande fã daquela cena final de 'Vingadores: Era de Ultron' entre o Visão e o Ultron —, fui direto para o Ultron", diz Terry Matalas, em entrevista ao g1 .

Conhecido pelo trabalho em "Star Trek: Picard", ele herdou o cargo de criador e roteirista de Jac Schaeffer ( "Viúva Negra" e "WandaVision"), que teve de focar no desenvolvimento de "Agatha".

"Eu tinha essa imagem dele vendo o Ultron, mas as outras pessoas não conseguiam vê-lo. E pensei: 'Bom, ele está dentro da cabeça dele'. Isso acabou levando ao conceito do espaço mental e à ideia de que havia outras inteligências artificiais naquela casa também. Mas, no sótão, vivia esse monstro de quem ele teve misericórdia."

Tamanho foco no vilão dependia da participação de Spader. Matalas não tinha plano B caso o intérprete original do robô – por mais que nunca tivesse mostrado o próprio rosto no filme – recusasse voltar ao papel.

Sem atuar desde 2023, com o fim da décima e última temporada de "Blacklist", o ator de 66 anos não tinha pressa para voltar a trabalhar.

"Eu estava exausto. Tinha feito dez anos de um projeto no qual se trabalhava sete dias por semana; era uma experiência totalmente imersiva e uma quantidade enorme de trabalho. Eu não sabia quando conseguiria me levantar da cama e voltar a trabalhar por um tempo", afirma Spader.

"Ainda estava me recuperando, na verdade. Aproveitando minha vida pessoal. Não sou nem um pouco um 'workaholic'. Fui lendo uma coisa ou outra, mas não encontrava nada com o que procuro em um trabalho."

"E o que procuro é sempre algo surpreendente, único, algo que realmente prenda minha atenção e pareça estranho e maravilhoso."

Foi quando Matalas fez o convite. Dessa vez, mais do que vestir uma roupa de captura e ser muito mau, ele poderia explorar outros lados do personagem – e mostrar a própria cara.

Afinal, como Matalas disse em outras entrevistas, de que adianta ter James Spader e não mostrar James Spader?

A colaboração com o produtor, principal responsável pelo "sim", também fez com que as gravações fossem mais prazerosas do que em "Era de Ultron".

"Eu me diverti mais, de verdade. Porque o que vocês não viram é o que acontecia entre as cenas ou entre os takes (risos) ou como chegávamos a certas decisões. Cada roteiro, cada história, eu e o Terry conversávamos sobre tudo. Passávamos por tudo, linha por linha, debatendo", conta ele.

Não à toa, os dois já falam sobre trabalhar juntos novamente – mesmo que por enquanto não se fale em uma segunda temporada.

"Foi um prazer imenso trabalhar com Paul, assim como com o Terry. Houve coisas que o Terry me disse algumas vezes durante a série que pareciam contraintuitivas para mim. Mas eu confiava no Terry, fazia, e sempre funcionava. Sempre dava certo", diz Spader.

"Fico muito feliz por termos isso gravado, porque vou usar da próxima vez em que trabalharmos juntos (risos). Da próxima vez em que eu for contraintuitivo, tenho isso registrado digitalmente. Por favor, garanta que vai nos enviar isso", retruca Matalas.

"Você sabe melhor do que ninguém que isso não vai ter efeito nenhum (risos)."

articles.title: Montadora de veículos do Paraná usa 'canhão antigranizo' internacional | G1
articles.standfirst: Renault Gelly do Brasil alega que, quatro anos após a instalação, só registrou queda de granizo uma vez. Apesar do relato, Simepar afirma que tecnologia não tem eficácia comprovada.
articles.summary: Renault Gelly do Brasil alega que, quatro anos após a instalação, só registrou queda de granizo uma vez. Apesar do relato, Simepar afirma que tecnologia não tem eficácia comprovada
articles.body:
A fabricante e montadora de veículos Renault Gelly do Brasil instalou uma tecnologia espanhola para evitar queda de granizo ao redor do Complexo Ayrton Senna, em São José dos Pinhais, na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba . Segundo a empresa, o 'canhão antigranizo' tem evitado danos nos cerca de 19 mil veículos estacionados diariamente nos pátios da montadora. Entenda abaixo.

De acordo com a montadora, a empresa tinha prejuízos de três a quatro vezes por ano devido a queda de granizo na região, até implementar a tecnologia internacional.

“A gente acompanhou os movimentos de fora, então a tecnologia veio de fora do Brasil, de uma empresa espanhola. Fora do Brasil já tinha esse sistema, e a gente estudou e implementou em 2022, e desde então a gente vê a eficiência dele. São quatro anos de instalação, hoje a gente tem dois sistemas e praticamente zero de granizo", contou Daniel Kaltmaier, gerente de logística da Renault Gelly do Brasil, entrevistado pela RPC, afiliada da TV Globo.

Canhão antigranizo foi instalado em montadora em 2022, em São José dos Pinhais. — Foto: Foto: RPC

Após a instalação da tecnologia, em 2022, a empresa registrou apenas um evento de temporal com queda de gelo, em janeiro deste ano. Segundo Kaltmaier, no episódio, os ventos fortes interferiram na eficácia da ferramenta.

O 'canhão antigranizo' promete proteger um raio de um quilômetro. A empresa instalou dois equipamentos para evitar danos nos veículos novos estacionados nos pátios da montadora.

Segundo a montadora, uma prestadora de serviços meteorológicos faz o monitoramento da região e envia um alerta para a previsão de formação de queda de granizo. Com isso, a Renault Gelly do Brasil pode acionar remotamente o 'canhão ', um equipamento instalado do lado de fora da fábrica.

O equipamento começa a 'disparar' ondas sonoras , uma espécie de 'tiro sônico', que provoca barulho e vibrações a cada 15 segundos. Essas ondas sonoras chegam até as nuvens carregadas e têm a missão de impedir a formação das pedras de gelo.

Apesar dos relatos da empresa, a Organização Meteorológica Mundial e o Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar) afirmaram que não há estudos suficientes que comprovam a eficácia do sistema contra a queda de granizo.

Acionamento do equipamento triplicou de 2025 para 2026

Segundo dados da empresa, o equipamento foi acionado 53 vezes em 2026 , um número três vezes maior do que no mesmo período (janeiro a outubro) do ano passado.

Conforme o meteorologista Marco Antonio Jusevicius, do Simepar, o aumento da incidência da queda de granizo na região se deve a uma combinação de fatores.

“Nós temos o El Niño funcionando, então ele potencializa os sistemas meteorológicos que causam a formação de tempestades que formam o granizo. Então o fato de ele estar aí, e a interação do cenário climático global, com os sistemas meteorológicos locais que favorecem a formação de tempestades, é isso que nós estamos observando”, explicou Jusevicius.

articles.title: Saudi OpenAI engineer arrested for planting hidden device to record executive meetings
articles.summary: A Saudi national and OpenAI engineer has been arrested by US federal agents and charged with allegedly installing a hidden audio recording device in an
articles.body: A Saudi national and OpenAI engineer has been arrested by US federal agents and charged with allegedly installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company to capture sensitive discussions about its technology, the US Justice Department said Tuesday.The employee, identified as 35-year-old Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested on Friday.The complaint did not name the company, but OpenAI confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices”. The company reported the discovery to the FBI and fired the employee.“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson was quoted as saying by AP.“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement read.The complaint does not specify what Alfozan intended to do with the recorded conversations. However, OpenAI said the device was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and equipped with advanced encryption and audio-monitoring capabilities.The company also said it had evidence that the employee planned to install additional listening devices in other parts of the office building to record meetings.Alfozan appeared in court for the first time on Tuesday. He faces a charge of using or attempting to use an electronic, mechanical or other device to intercept oral communications.According to the complaint, the recording device was found on September 30, concealed in toilet paper and plugged into a USB port at the back of a television in an executive conference room.The conference room did not have a security camera when the device was installed. However, CCTV footage from other parts of the office showed Alfozan near the room on nearly a dozen occasions last month, despite having no authority to access the space or attend meetings there, the complaint said.OpenAI later installed a camera in the room. According to the FBI, footage recorded last week showed Alfozan entering the room and checking behind the television where the device had been placed.The complaint also alleges that Alfozan used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company's building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities and calendars.Days before his arrest last week, Alfozan allegedly left an unattended bag in another room. When OpenAI personnel opened it, they found his wallet, identification documents and another recording device similar to the one discovered in the executive conference room, the complaint said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: BHOPAL: After spending eight months cleaning the Ajnar River in Madhya Pradesh, environmental activist and content creator Bittu Tabahi has returned to find garbage dumped along its banks again.In an Instagram video, Bittu expressed disappointment over the river’s condition and showed himself removing waste once more, prompting social media users to question the lack of civic sense and praise his continued efforts."I never imagined that eight months of my hard work would go to waste like this," Bittu wrote as the caption of the video shared on Instagram.Bittu Tabahi returns to clean Ajnar RiverBittu explained that he carries his own equipment and wears gloves before beginning the cleanup to protect himself. articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed that intelligence and military chiefs feared waking him on the night of October 7, 2023, believing
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed that intelligence and military chiefs feared waking him on the night of October 7, 2023, believing he could inadvertently trigger a Hamas attack, as he again blamed the security establishment for failing to anticipate the assault.“If we wake up the prime minister, he’ll cause Hamas to attack us without meaning to,” Netanyahu asserted the security chiefs believed, as quoted by The Times of Israel.Netanyahu said security officials had mistaken Hamas’s preparations for a military drill or a minor attack, despite signs that the Palestinian militant group was preparing for an assault.According to Netanyahu, officials had seen Hamas operatives putting Israeli SIM cards into their phones and senior Hamas commanders heading underground. However, he said in the Channel 14 interview that, “they were locked in a conception that it was a drill, or a small thing.”Netanyahu claimed that had he been alerted, he would have ordered a stronger response before the attack unfolded.“If they had woken me up, they knew I’d have woken everybody and canceled Nova and put the air force on alert,” he said, referring to the Nova music festival, where hundreds of people were killed during the Hamas-led October 7 assault.The prime minister has repeatedly blamed Israel’s security establishment for the failures surrounding the attack, while denying that he received and ignored advance warnings of a major assault from Gaza.Egyptian spy chief’s visitNetanyahu also confirmed reports that Egyptian intelligence chief Abbas Kamel had secretly flown to Israel days before the October 7 attack. Kamel reportedly warned Israeli officials that Hamas was planning a major assault if Israel did not agree to a deal involving the release of prisoners and economic concessions.Netanyahu, however, denied meeting or speaking with Kamel during the visit and said he did not know whom the Egyptian intelligence chief had met.“He didn’t meet with me,” Netanyahu said, adding that he had been attending a memorial ceremony for Israeli soldiers at the time.“He didn’t meet with me, he didn’t speak with me,” he continued. “When does an intelligence chief meet with a head of state?”“The head of the Egyptian intelligence was here. He spent something like 50 minutes on the ground. I want to know who he met,” Netanyahu said.When reports of the warning emerged, Netanyahu had issued a statement saying, “No early message came from Egypt and the prime minister did not speak or meet with the intelligence chief since the establishment of the government, not indirectly or directly.”The reports about Kamel’s visit are among several allegations that Netanyahu received advance warnings of a possible Hamas attack but failed to act on them. He has denied the allegations and attributed the intelligence failures to security officials.Netanyahu also rejected claims that he had blocked a viable Gaza deal that could have secured the earlier return of hostages and saved the lives of some who died in captivity. articles.summary: A cyberattack that hijacked commercial refrigeration units across hundreds of French supermarkets has offered a real-world demonstration of the dangers
articles.body: A cyberattack that hijacked commercial refrigeration units across hundreds of French supermarkets has offered a real-world demonstration of the dangers lurking in connected infrastructure. For European officials, the incident does more than spotlight digital vulnerabilities in the food supply – it provides a warning and fuel to growing anxieties across the region that internet-linked transit systems, including hundreds of public buses built by Chinese manufacturers, could be remotely immobilised right on the roads during a crisis.The French refrigerator attackThe Paris prosecutor’s office launched an investigation this week following an overnight cyberattack targeting cooling systems across multiple French grocery chains. Attackers breached central management panels, overriding controls to force refrigeration and freezer units into non-stop defrost cycles at 50°C (122°F). This resulted in fires, melted equipment and dumpsters full of spoiled food, with French retail group Les Mousquetaires (operator of Intermarché and Netto) reporting losses reaching millions of euros.France’s National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) confirmed the attack targeted Danfoss AK-SC and AK-SM series controllers. Danfoss acknowledged the breach, stating the affected units ran “outdated firmware” and noting that it “long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions.”Echoing Europe’s nightmare over Chinese connected busesThe supermarket breach underscores a core vulnerability: once a piece of infrastructure is connected online for diagnostics, anyone with system-level access – whether a malicious hacker or the manufacturer itself – can override its physical operations.That exact mechanism was at the heart of the panic in Scandinavia, where transport operators in Denmark and Norway, last year, started probing Chinese-built electric buses over fears they could be remotely weaponized or shut down.Scrutiny centered on Yutong, the Zhengzhou-based company that ranks as the world’s largest bus maker by sales volume. Danish transport operator Movia, which runs 262 Yutong buses across Copenhagen and eastern Denmark, warned that over-the-air (OTA) functionality creates severe exposure.“Because these buses can receive updates and diagnostic tests 'over the air,' they can be stopped remotely, either by the manufacturer or by a hacker,” Movia COO Jeppe Gaard told NBC News.Norwegian transit agency Ruter, which oversees half of Norway’s public transport, conducted controlled tests “inside a mountain” comparing Yutong vehicles against Dutch-made VDL models. While Dutch buses lacked automated OTA functions, Yutong maintained “direct digital access to each individual bus,” leading Ruter to conclude that the fleet could, in theory, be rendered completely inoperable by the manufacturer.In response, Yutong stressed that it “strictly complies with the applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards,” noting that its European Union operational data is encrypted and housed in an Amazon Web Services facility in Frankfurt, Germany.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A 153-acre Scottish Highland estate with a private loch, river, deer stalking and trout fishing rights is now on the market for offers over £800,000.
articles.body: A 153-acre Scottish Highland estate with a private loch, river, deer stalking and trout fishing rights is now on the market for offers over £800,000. Located in Glen Cannich, Inverness-shire, Craskie offers a rare opportunity to own a Highland property combining a family home, holiday cottage, glamping pods, grazing land and woodland. The estate could appeal to buyers seeking a rural retreat, a holiday rental business or land for conservation and environmental projects. With its mix of residential accommodation, tourism potential and traditional Highland sporting rights, Craskie stands out among Scottish estates for sale. Here is a closer look at the property, its features and the opportunities it offers prospective buyers.What 153 acres of Highland land includes: Grazing, woodland, Loch Craskie, and the River CannichAccording to the PrimeLocation listing from the selling agent Strutt & Parker, Craskie extends to approximately 153.55 acres, or 62.14 hectares, in total. The listing describes grazing land and amenity woodlands, and states that ownership includes Loch Craskie and the River Cannich. Strutt & Parker describes the property as an easily managed small estate with a mix of residential, tourism, sporting, forestry, and environmental opportunities. It also highlights woodland creation and natural capital opportunities. The estate sits about 32 miles west of Inverness in Glen Cannich, close to the well-known glens of Affric and Strathfarrar, in an area where land and smaller estates are rarely available. The listing adds that a grazing lease in favour of a third party affects part of the estate for a remaining term of 55 years.What the homes include: Craskie House, the Old Mill cottage, and the remains of the original houseCraskie House was constructed in the 1970s and is of modern construction under tile roofs, according to the listing. Its headline features call it a detached three-bedroom house, while the room breakdown lists three bedrooms on the ground floor and two more on the first floor, alongside a sitting room, dining room, kitchen, two bathrooms, and a utility room. Immediately behind it stands the Old Mill, a former mill house with traditional stone walls and a corrugated metal roof, which has two bedrooms and is currently used for holiday lets. The listing also notes the remains of the original Craskie house next door, which offer an opportunity for redevelopment, subject to all relevant consents being obtained. Buyers should confirm details directly with Strutt & Parker.How glamping pods and a shepherd's hut offer tourism opportunities at a Scottish loch-side estateAccording to the listing, four wooden pods are already in place, positioned to take advantage of stunning, uninterrupted views over Loch Craskie. Each pod has a large decked terrace, and planning permission exists for an additional four pods and an associated amenity block. Guests would share heated bathroom facilities in an annexe of the main house, which the listing says include luxury showers, toilets, a shared fridge freezer, and a dishwashing area. The listing also mentions a short-term let shepherd's hut, and it notes that the Old Mill is currently used for holiday lets. Strutt & Parker presents this mix as tourism diversification. The listing also notes a right of pre-emption over the property in favour of a neighbouring estate, with further details available from the selling agents.Deer stalking, wild brown trout fishing, and nearby Inverness, what sporting rights and location offerThe listing highlights roe, red, and sika deer stalking and wild brown trout fishing, and it lists stalking, fishing, horse riding, hill walking, and mountain biking among the outdoor pursuits available within the landholding and locally. The village of Cannich has local services including a convenience store, while Beauly offers a delicatessen, café, butcher, and a tweed and knitwear manufacturer and retailer. Inverness is the commercial centre of the Highlands, and Inverness Airport, 37 miles east, provides daily flights to London. Beauly has a railway station with frequent services to Inverness, where trains run to Edinburgh and Glasgow and a sleeper service to London. articles.title: Lying atop woman, sans backing proof, can't be held as rape: Patna high court
articles.summary: PATNA: Patna HC has reduced a man's rape conviction to indecent assault, ruling that allegations of him entering a woman's hut at night, covering her
articles.body: PATNA: Patna HC has reduced a man's rape conviction to indecent assault, ruling that allegations of him entering a woman's hut at night, covering her mouth and mounting her body, without supporting medical or material evidence, were insufficient to establish rape.A single-judge bench of Justice Sandeep Kumar passed the verdict on Oct 8 while partly allowing a criminal appeal by Mohammad Ainul Haq.The judgement became public Tuesday. According to the prosecution, Haq entered the woman's hut around 10pm on Feb 8, 2010, covered her mouth and mounted her "with evil intentions".When he removed his hand, she raised an alarm, drawing 10-15 villagers, including her immediate neighbour, who caught him.During the trial, all witnesses except the woman turned hostile. The prosecution produced no medical evidence, such as bruises or injuries, or material evidence, such as torn or disarranged clothes, to support the allegation.The high court held that even if the woman's testimony was accepted, the evidence established, at best, criminal trespass and assault, not rape.HC accordingly modified a Begusarai trial court's July 29, 2013, verdict convicting Haq of raping a widow and sentencing him to four years in prison and a fine.However, the court held him guilty of assault on a woman with an intent to outrage her modesty and imposed a fine of Rs 25,000, payable to the woman within three weeks.Justice Kumar relied on Supreme Court rulings in Aman Kumar vs State of Haryana (2004) and Rupan Deol Bajaj vs KPS Gill (1995).You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.summary: Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina has called Dhaka's decision to skip the Brics summit in India “deeply unfortunate”, saying the country's
articles.body: Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina has called Dhaka's decision to skip the Brics summit in India “deeply unfortunate”, saying the country's participation could have opened new opportunities for its economic and social development.“Foreign policy cannot be conducted through personal reaction or short-term political calculation,” Hasina told PTI, commenting on Bangladesh's absence from the summit.'Relations between two countries can't be determined by personal considerations or political sensitivities involving one individual,' she added.She also said Bangladesh was facing a serious national crisis, adding that “Bangladesh is passing through a grave national crisis and democratic space has been closed. Bangladesh needs a mature, balanced and confident foreign policy. A responsible government should open doors for the country, not close them."Meanwhile, the Indian government has reiterated that it invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to attend the BRICS summit as chair of BIMSTEC and also extended a separate invitation for a bilateral visit.In a letter dated July 14, accessed by TOI, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had invited Rahman to the summit in his capacity as BIMSTEC chair, saying his participation would “greatly enrich the deliberations”. Modi also noted that the summit was of special significance as it marked 20 years since the formal establishment of Brics.After Rahman was sworn in as prime minister, Modi invited him for a bilateral visit. However, Dhaka subsequently withdrew from talks to finalise the dates, apparently due to the lack of a firm commitment from India on the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) was responding to Dhaka's claim that the invitation for the summit had been extended to the BIMSTEC chair and not Rahman.“I have said this before as well, we had invited the PM of Bangladesh on a bilateral visit. articles.title: Is Netanyahu urging Trump to strike Iran before US, Israel elections? What new report reveals
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump discussed the possibility of launching a major joint operation against Iran before
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump discussed the possibility of launching a major joint operation against Iran before elections in both countries, with Netanyahu raising concerns about Tehran's efforts to rebuild its nuclear programme, according to an Axios report citing US and Israeli officials and other sources familiar with the matter.The discussions took place last week, before Trump said he would not strike Iran ahead of the US midterm elections.The report said Netanyahu had held several calls with Trump over the past two weeks about resuming major combat operations against Iran.According to an Israeli official cited in the report, Netanyahu told Trump he was concerned about Israeli intelligence suggesting that Iran was taking troubling steps to reconstitute its nuclear programme. Israel is particularly worried about the possibility of Iran operating Pickaxe Mountain as a uranium enrichment site.The two leaders discussed a potential joint US-Israeli operation targeting Iranian military and nuclear facilities, the report said.However, the White House disputed the account that Trump and Netanyahu had discussed resuming the war. A White House official called the report's claim "false", adding, "The President has said that we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections."Netanyahu's office said the prime minister maintained regular contact with Trump and senior US administration officials but did not comment on the content of their conversations.Trump weighs optionsAccording to the report, Trump initially appeared inclined to resume attacks but later grew more hesitant. A US official said the president had been going back and forth on the issue."Bibi seems to want to go in again. He has talked to the president about it a couple times, and the president has said, 'Well, you know, Bibi, go ahead and get ready.' But there's really no commitment. 'Go ahead and get ready' is maybe now, maybe later, maybe never," Axios quoted the official as saying.US defence secretary Pete Hegseth and the leadership of US Central Command are the strongest supporters of renewed strikes, a source familiar with the discussions told Axios. Most of Trump's advisers, however, favour continuing economic sanctions and other forms of pressure for now."They claim this economic choking is working better and better. Let's keep it up," a second US official said.Trump's senior cabinet members had also met for hours at Camp David on October 2 to discuss the next steps in the war and the possibility of resuming strikes, the report said.Despite uncertainty over the decision, the Israeli and US militaries remain on alert and are completing preparations to be ready if Trump changes his position, according to the sources cited by Axios.Election risksA renewed military campaign could have significant consequences for both leaders ahead of the Israeli elections on October 27 and the US midterm elections a week later.Iran could retaliate by firing hundreds of ballistic missiles at Israel, potentially disrupting the Israeli election process.According to a source briefed on a call, Israeli military chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir spoke last week with US Joint Chiefs Chairman General Dan Caine about the possibility of resuming full-scale fighting against Iran within the next three weeks.Zamir said a resumption of hostilities within that timeframe could lead to the Israeli elections being postponed because of the likely Iranian retaliation, the report said. Caine's spokesman, Joe Holstead, declined to comment.The report also highlighted concerns that a strike before the elections could be perceived as a political move by Netanyahu, potentially undermining public trust in the Israeli military, which is widely viewed as apolitical.One US official said the White House was aware of Netanyahu's domestic political calculations."Bibi's got an election before the midterms. He believes his strength is being a wartime prime minister," the official said as per the report.However, an Israeli official told Axios that Netanyahu had recently told his security and intelligence chiefs that Trump, rather than Netanyahu, had initiated the discussion about a possible attack before the elections.According to that account, Trump had asked Netanyahu whether Israel would join the operation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Young Jain Professionals convention blends Silicon Valley innovation with Jain values
articles.summary: MILPITAS, California: More than 300 people, including spiritual leaders, technology executives, entrepreneurs, investors and young professionals, attended
articles.body: MILPITAS, California: More than 300 people, including spiritual leaders, technology executives, entrepreneurs, investors and young professionals, attended the four-day Young Jain Professionals (YJP) Convention 2026, which concluded here on October 12.Held at the Embassy Suites under the theme “Reinventing Your Wheel,” the convention brought together participants to explore innovation, career development, networking and Jain philosophy. The program featured keynote addresses, technology discussions, professional development workshops, cultural performances and a startup pitch competition, according to the official program guide.YJP is an initiative of the Federation of Jain Associations in North America (JAINA), an umbrella organization dedicated to preserving, practicing and promoting Jain religious values and the Jain way of life.The gathering drew prominent speakers from the fields of philanthropy, technology and investment, including Dr. Jasvant Modi, a leading Jain philanthropist and driving force behind the establishment of Jain academic chairs worldwide; Kanwal Rekhi, a pioneering Silicon Valley investor; Arvind Jain, founder and CEO of Glean; Rajen Sheth, chairman of Boardwalk Development Group; and Deep Nishar, former managing director at General Catalyst.Jain spiritual leaders, including Rushiji Hem Vijay Maharaj and Dr. Arun Vijay Maharaj, also addressed the gathering, underscoring the convention’s emphasis on integrating professional growth with Jain spiritual traditions and principles.Sunny Jain, a project manager at Goldman Sachs in Dallas, described the convention as an opportunity for Jain professionals from across the United States and Canada to connect, exchange ideas and support one another’s professional growth.“[It] has been an incredible forum to bring Jains across the nation United States and Canada to come together in a place where we can connect with like-minded people, learn about Jain values, connect on a professional level, how can we leverage mentorship, leverage our contact and be able to help each other grow in this community,” he said.Jain, who served on the organization’s board in 2018 and 2019, told The American Bazaar that the convention offered valuable opportunities to learn from accomplished members of the community.He said he attended “some incredible session” and listened “to some great leaders and speakers in our community that have succeeded and are willing to share that wisdom with others in our community.”Technology and entrepreneurshipTechnology and innovation figured prominently in the convention’s program, reflecting the growing influence of Jain professionals in Silicon Valley and other technology hubs.A panel titled “TECHnically Speaking” explored emerging trends and developments in the technology sector. Panelists included Anand Oswal, executive vice president and general manager of AI and network security at Palo Alto Networks; Lavina Kavediya, a product leader specializing in consumer AI and retail technology; and Dr. Nikunj Mehta, founder and CEO of Falkonry.The discussion covered a range of topics, including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, consumer technology, industrial Internet of Things (IoT) applications and machine learning.Entrepreneurship was another major focus, highlighted by the YJP Shark Tank pitch competition on Oct. 11. The top three winners received cash prizes of $5,001, $2,501 and $1,501, respectively.Prithvion, founded by plant scientist Aishwarya Kothari, won the competition. The company is developing a biology-aware disease prediction platform that forecasts fungal disease risk up to seven days before symptoms appear. By integrating pathogen kinetics, host crop phenology and hyperlocal microclimate data, the platform aims to help growers determine when the risk of disease warrants spraying and when treatment can be skipped.Kothari, who has a background in synthetic biology and cellular agriculture, founded Prithvion to address the gap between growers’ needs and the capabilities of generic agricultural technology tools.The judging panel included Sahil Kothari, an entrepreneur, investor and mentor; Mansi Shah, a law partner and technology investor; Deep Nishar; Pranjal Daga, founder of Accend and a participant in Y Combinator’s Summer 2023 cohort; and Priyanka Shah, a life sciences portfolio lead and venture adviser.Professional development and Jain philosophyBeyond technology and entrepreneurship, the convention placed considerable emphasis on personal growth and professional development, with two sets of breakout sessions designed to encourage participants to reflect on their careers and broaden their perspectives.The Oct. 10 workshop, titled “Re-Calibrating…,” explored Jain philosophical concepts such as karma and rebirth, alongside topics including creative expression, personal identity, confidence and improvisation. The sessions sought to connect philosophical reflection with professional and personal development.A second workshop, “Circling Back Forward,” held on October 11, covered a wide range of topics, from agentic and physical AI to venture capital, decision-making and Ayurveda.One session examined Anekantavada, the Jain principle of multiple perspectives, and how it could be applied to identifying investment opportunities in venture capital.Other sessions explored what makes startups attractive to investors and how Jain values can guide decisions involving business strategy and environmental impact.The program also included a structured networking initiative titled “Chain Reaction,” designed to connect attendees with potential mentors and industry leaders through guided discussions and speed-networking sessions.Cultural celebrationsAlongside its professional development sessions, the convention offered cultural and social events that brought participants together outside formal discussions.The opening evening featured “Pacific Coast Hungama,” a talent show showcasing music and entertainment. Saturday’s festivities included “Raas in the Redwoods,” a Garba Night celebration, while the closing evening featured the “Golden State Gala.”Shikha Kothari, an adviser to Young Jain Professionals, highlighted the diversity of talent on display.“It’s very cool to see the people who are poets, we had from different angles, and we had some beautiful classical pieces, [and] we had fusion pieces,” she said.Featured performers included Jai Loonker, a dancer, choreographer and engineer, and Priya Puram, an Indian American stand-up comedian and product manager based in San Francisco.For Apeksha Shah, an Orange, California, resident who immigrated to the United States from Godhra, Gujarat, Garba Night was among the convention’s highlights.“It was very amazing,” she said.Shah particularly enjoyed the opportunity to celebrate with participants who had come from different parts of India, including Mumbai and Gujarat.Plant-based diningFood was another highlight of the convention, which served a plant-based Jain menu throughout the four days, offering participants a variety of Indian and international dishes.The selections included poha and chia pudding for breakfast, a Mexican-themed lunch, an Indo-Chinese dinner, pani puri, corn chaat, Mediterranean falafel and Thai cuisine.Priyanka Chordia, founder of D’Deco Jewels, who oversaw the planning and coordination of more than 13 meals and snacks during the convention, said the organizers wanted to use the event to promote greater awareness of vegan food.“Last year we had decided that, in our convention, we will emphasize the importance of vegan food along with Jain food,” she said.“Through this journey, we realized that many people are not aware of veganism and how to prepare vegan food at home. Through the convention, our aim was to not only feed people but to raise awareness that you can do all cuisines and all dishes vegan.”Chordia, who is based in New York, said coordinating the food arrangements for a convention in the San Francisco Bay Area presented logistical challenges. However, working with Hasmukh and Kavita Patel of Utsav Kitchen, the team managed to serve 13 meals over four days without repeating dishes.The menu spanned Indian, Mexican, Mediterranean, Indo-Chinese and Thai cuisines, along with a wide selection of desserts, including vegan falooda.For Sunny Jain, a Dallas resident, the food was among the most memorable aspects of the gathering.“My highlights have been the food,” he said. “I think the food has been absolutely incredible. It’s been a you know fully plant-based and you know being able to eat everything and it’s been absolutely delicious.”The convention concluded on October 12 with a closing ceremony and lunch, followed by a visit to the Jain Center of Northern California.(Jayujyoti Mullik contributed to this report. articles.title: US Department of Homeland Security removes 540-day grace period for immigrants after their work authorisation expires; here's what the new rules say
articles.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has moved to permanently end a policy that allowed many immigrants to continue working for up to 540 days
articles.body: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has moved to permanently end a policy that allowed many immigrants to continue working for up to 540 days after their employment authorisation expired while renewal applications were pending, according to a Bloomberg Law report. The final rule, released this week, makes permanent an interim measure introduced last year that scrapped the Biden-era 540-day automatic extension period for certain categories of foreign workers. The change is set to take effect when it is published in the Federal Register on October 14.What the rule says* The automatic extension of work permits during renewal is eliminated, so workers lose authorization when their permit expires, even if a renewal is pending.* The final rule takes effect when it is published in the Federal Register on Oct. 14.* Foreign workers cannot apply to renew their documents until 180 days before expiration.Why the 540-day extension existedThe extension window was designed to ensure immigrant workers were not pushed out of jobs because of processing delays at US Citizenship and Immigration Services. The agency has since added a number of hurdles under the Trump administration for immigrants to keep or renew their employment authorization.Who will be affectedThe policy affects several groups of immigrants who rely on Employment Authorisation Documents (EADs), including asylum seekers and spouses of H-1B visa holders on H-4 visas. DHS said the move would enable more frequent vetting of applicants seeking employment authorisation. The agency argues that shorter extension periods allow authorities to conduct updated eligibility and security reviews more regularly.USCIS faces large backlogDespite the change, USCIS continues to deal with significant renewal delays.According to agency data cited by Bloomberg Law, more than 432,000 work permit renewal applications had been pending for six months or longer as of June 30. Of those, more than 91,000 applications had been awaiting a decision for over 18 months.At the same time, foreign workers are generally not permitted to file renewal applications more than 180 days before their current work permits expire, limiting their ability to offset lengthy processing times.Legal challenge aheadThe policy has already faced legal scrutiny. A group of H-4 visa holders filed a lawsuit against DHS in January, arguing that the agency's decision to end the longer automatic extension period violated the Administrative Procedure Act. Last month, a federal judge in California issued a limited injunction blocking enforcement of the interim rule against the plaintiffs involved in the case. The court found that DHS had not adequately followed procedural requirements and failed to address the reliance interests of affected individuals.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Trespassing, filed by the JD(U)?” Gawande said, calling it a “sad day for the JD(U) and an even sadder day for Indian democracy”.Das and Ranka were detained early Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, recently denotified as a designated protest site, while raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar designated Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as venues for demonstrations, removing Jantar Mantar from the list of approved protest sites. articles.title: Israel election paradox as parties winning no seats could decide who forms government
articles.summary: Israel’s election could turn on a political paradox with parties that fail to win a single seat could determine who forms the next government.
articles.body: Israel’s election could turn on a political paradox with parties that fail to win a single seat could determine who forms the next government.With Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition short of a projected parliamentary majority, smaller parties hovering around the minimum vote threshold could decide the balance of power, according to an analysis by The Times of Israel.Israel’s recent electoral history offers a clear example of how parties failing to cross the threshold can reshape the political outcome. The country held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 amid repeated failures by rival political camps to secure stable parliamentary majorities.According to The Times of Israel, Netanyahu’s bloc faces the risk of losing crucial seats if smaller right-wing parties fail to cross the electoral threshold. The report highlights parties hovering around the 3.25 per cent mark, where even a small shortfall could leave their votes without parliamentary representation.The opposition faces a similar challenge, as some smaller parties are also struggling to secure enough support to enter the Knesset. However, the report suggests that the immediate risk of threshold-related losses could be greater for Netanyahu’s camp.How Israel’s election system worksIsrael follows a nationwide proportional representation system in which voters elect party lists to the 120-member Knesset, the country’s parliament.Parties must secure at least 3.25 per cent of the valid vote to win seats. Those falling below the threshold receive no representation, and their votes are excluded from seat allocation.The prime minister is not directly elected. A party leader must assemble a coalition commanding the support of at least 61 lawmakers to form a government.This makes smaller parties crucial, as their success or failure to cross the threshold can alter the parliamentary arithmetic and determine which bloc has a path to power.How small parties could determine the election resultSmall parties could decide whether Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or the opposition gets enough seats to form the next government.Under Israel’s election rules, a party must win at least 3.25 per cent of the vote to enter parliament. If it falls short, it gets no seats, and the votes cast for it do not count towards seat allocation. This can hurt the larger political bloc that the party could have supported.The 2022 election offers an example with the Left-wing Meretz and Arab-led Balad failed to cross the threshold and won no seats. Netanyahu’s bloc secured 64 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, giving him a parliamentary majority and allowing him to return as prime minister.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Forget the saree! Indian jewellery is having its own craft revival, and here's what's changing
articles.summary: History has regarded the saree as one of India’s most visible cultural canvases, a living expression of inherited identity, regional textile traditions
articles.body: History has regarded the saree as one of India’s most visible cultural canvases, a living expression of inherited identity, regional textile traditions and artisanal skill. However, in today’s modern world, the conversation has broadened. The rich Indian heritage and its craftsmanship are being treasured, reinterpreted and presented to a contemporary audience through another equally impactful medium: jewellery. Rhea Poddar Loyalka, Creative Director, Deshya by Ma Passion, shares insights on the changes jewellery in India is undergoing.This shift has widely influenced the way luxury is perceived. There is a significant rise in the desire for depth and meaning. Material rarity alone does not solely define value; what does is the sum of refined skill, cultural context and human connection engraved within an object. With the landscape changing, the spotlight has also moved towards traditional techniques used in Indian jewellery. Kundan, Meenakari, Jadau, Thewa, Filigree, etc. have garnered renewed relevance and are no longer reserved for important ceremonies or confined to archival collections. They are being reimagined as sculptural silhouettes, versatile everyday pieces and modern heirlooms designed for modern consumers today.For example, Meenakari, always known only as an intricate reverse detail, is moving beyond its conventional role. The aesthetic of contemporary designs is being led by colour, geometry and the hand-painted art of bright Meenakari and its luminous enamel surface. Carved gemstones, which have long been associated with royalty and historic ateliers, are being revamped into cocktail rings, bold earrings and sculptural pendants. These reinterpretations aren’t a nostalgic practice to relive history, but an act of achieving meaningful permanence through creative perpetuity.The driving force of this movement is the artisan. The Karigar, whose identity has long remained a secret, has finally taken centre stage with jewellery’s contemporary evolution. There is knowledge in every calibrated gemstone, hand-applied layer of enamel and precisely executed gold detail that has withstood the test of time. With luxury and craftsmanship joining forces through increased collaborations between premium brands and artisanal communities, the designer-craftsperson relationship is strengthening as a result. This sheds light on the karigar, all the while making the relationship invaluable.With fame and visibility comes great responsibility. It is important for revival not to be driven by mere romanticism, and to stay respectfully rooted. With meaningful craft-led design should come fair recognition, sustainable livelihoods and opportunities for artisans to grow their practice. Traditional skills can be bridged to contemporary markets through institutional initiatives such as artisan identification, cluster development and design training.Heritage being economically strengthened and not merely showcased will narrate the next phase of India’s jewellery story.In this transformation, consumers are active participants too. Present-day jewellery connoisseurs seek meaning and uniqueness in their pieces, with distinctive techniques and unusual material combinations. Jewellery today isn’t a mere investment made to leave an impression for a certain occasion, but a personal medium of expression that allows the world a glimpse into one’s identity. Jewellery is versatile yet impactful, and can be worn with a saree, a plain white shirt or a tailored suit.Jewellery today is not merely an accessory, but wearable craft, cultural memory and contemporary design in equal measure. Innovation is at the core of Indian craft revival, with artisans, designers and luxury houses continuing to work across disciplines. Certainly, Indian heritage is setting a new narrative in the language of jewellery. It’s memorable in the present while being rooted and paving the way for the future.You use AI every day. articles.title: SJM urges Centre to block Starlink’s rollout
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM) on Tuesday urged the Centre to block Starlink’s commercial rollout, questioning whether Elon Musk’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM) on Tuesday urged the Centre to block Starlink’s commercial rollout, questioning whether Elon Musk’s satellite broadband service could ensure that Indian traffic passes through domestic gateways and comply with orders to restrict connectivity in specified areas.SJM national co-convener Ashwani Mahajan said the concerns involved India’s capacity to monitor communications lawfully and enforce security restrictions. It argued that laser links between satellites could allow traffic to bypass Indian ground infrastructure and travel through foreign networks.“A key regulatory condition is that Starlink must be able to precisely restrict its services at the govt’s behest,” SJM said. It questioned whether the company could meet this requirement, citing terrorism, riots and protests as situations in which authorities may seek local shutdowns.At issue, in SJM’s argument, is whether Indian authorities can enforce security directives on a foreign operator whose network extends beyond the country’s physical borders. SJM contrasted this with incumbent telecom companies which, it said, cooperate with investigators and can suspend services in designated areas.The group accused Musk of applying public pressure instead of addressing Indian security concerns. Its intervention follows his allegation that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink to protect their businesses and his criticism of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani.SJM also flagged potential misuse by insurgents and smugglers. Starlink equipment was recovered during a drug seizure in Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army search operation in Manipur in 2024. Musk has maintained that Starlink’s satellite beams were never activated over India.Starlink received a telecom licence on June 6, 2025, and authorisation from space regulator IN-SPACe on July 8 that year. Its commercial launch awaits completion of security assessments and spectrum assignment.On Oct 8, the communications ministry rejected the discrimination allegations as “baseless and misconceived”, saying Starlink, Jio’s satellite venture and Bharti-backed OneWeb were at broadly the same regulatory stage. Each must demonstrate security compliance before seeking spectrum, it said.Starlink has previously said Indian user data would remain within the country and its security controls would meet Indian requirements.Arguing for indigenous alternatives, SJM claimed blocking Starlink would accelerate domestic satellite broadband development and eventually deliver cheaper connectivity to remote areas. It said India’s growing space capabilities and private sector participation could support domestic alternatives, even if their rollout took some more time. It also invoked US trade restrictions, arguing India was entitled to withhold permission on national security grounds.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
